record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.original_question: How do core concepts and equilibrium notions behave in large markets with asymmetric information, especially with respect to core convergence and the way information is transmitted or revealed through market interaction and blocking mechanisms?

evidence.quote: Given how important it is to understand information flows in markets, more research along these lines is definitely needed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an exchange economy with a finite set of agents $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$, a commodity space $\mathbb{R}^\ell_+$, and a finite set $\Omega$ of states of nature. Each agent $i$ has a state-dependent utility function $u_i:\mathbb{R}^\ell_+\times\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$, an initial endowment map $e_i:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^\ell_+$, a private information partition $\mathcal{F}_i$ of $\Omega$, and a prior probability $\pi_i$ on $\Omega$. An allocation is a profile $(x_i)_{i\in N}$ of state-contingent consumption plans satisfying $\sum_i x_i(\omega)=\sum_i e_i(\omega)$ for every $\omega$. For a coalition $S\subseteq N$, various core notions (the private core, the coarse core, the fine core, and the core with respect to equilibrium blocking, in which information transmission inside a blocking coalition is modeled as the equilibrium of a communication mechanism) prescribe which allocations $S$ can credibly block, taking into account measurability with respect to pooled or individual information.

For $r\geq 1$ let the $r$-fold replica economy $\mathcal{E}^r$ consist of $r$ copies of each agent in $N$, with the same utilities, endowments, information partitions, and priors. Let $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ denote a chosen interim core notion (for instance the core with respect to equilibrium blocking) and let $W^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ denote the set of incentive-compatible Walrasian (rational expectations) equilibrium allocations of $\mathcal{E}^r$.

Provide a complete characterization of the asymptotic relationship between $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ and $W^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ as $r\to\infty$. Specifically:

(a) Identify necessary and sufficient conditions on $(u_i,e_i,\mathcal{F}_i,\pi_i)_{i\in N}$ under which every sequence of equal-treatment allocations $(x^r)$ with $x^r\in\mathrm{C}^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ converges (in an appropriate sense) to an element of $W^*$, i.e., the chosen core converges to the set of incentive-compatible Walrasian allocations.

(b) Identify necessary and sufficient conditions under which core convergence fails, in the sense that asymmetric information persists as an externality and a non-vanishing gap remains between $\mathrm{C}^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ and $W^*(\mathcal{E}^r)$ as $r\to\infty$.

(c) Determine, for the core with respect to equilibrium blocking, exactly how much of the agents' private information is endogenously transmitted or revealed within blocking coalitions in the limit, and relate this to the informational content of the limiting price system.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Forges, Minelli and Vohra (2002) and subsequent work establish that the coarse core fails to converge to price equilibrium allocations in replicated economies with asymmetric information, while other contributions provide sufficient conditions for convergence under specific core notions (e.g., equilibrium blocking, private core in quasilinear settings). However, a complete characterization of when core convergence holds or fails across the various interim core notions, and a full understanding of endogenous information transmission via blocking in the limit, has not been achieved and is described as needing further research.

status_evidence.title: On the Failure of Core Convergence in Economies with Asymmetric Information
status_evidence.snippet: In interim economies with asymmetric information, the coarse core of Wilson (1978) does not converge to price equilibrium allocations as the economy is replicated.
status_evidence.claim: Core convergence fails for the coarse core under asymmetric information, indicating only partial understanding of when convergence holds.

status_evidence.title: Core convergence with asymmetric information
status_evidence.snippet: Information transmission in large interim quasilinear economies via the core with respect to equilibrium blocking; conditions for convergence to incentive compatible ex-post Walrasian allocations.
status_evidence.claim: Sufficient conditions for convergence are known in special cases, but a full characterization across general core notions remains open.
